u295.description: The unit responds to tokens that continue domain-specific multi-token terms: disease/biology abbreviations and adjectives (leukemic, CML, PML, epigenetic, superoxide) and British-spelled verbs like 'equalised'/'evacuated'/'reciprocate', often at word-internal or term-continuation positions.

u296.description: No single shared concept or role is evident; the marked tokens span diverse topics and grammatical contexts.

u297.description: Nouns that are proper-noun modifiers denoting nationality, ethnicity, or culture (American, German, Chinese, Thai, Canadian, etc.) modifying a following noun.

u298.description: The unit responds to the 'g' in words/names related to Glee (e.g., glee club, glee) or, more broadly, to the letter 'g' within English words, especially in foreign-language or proper-name contexts.

u299.description: Completes or continues common English words and multiword expressions, especially compound terms (Archduke, medley, catechism, unstable) and fixed phrases (put forth, unknownst, insufficiently).

u300.description: The unit fires on many distinct content words (immigrated, riots, grounds, 侗, pear, presses, etc.), with no single shared concept, grammar role, or next-word pattern linking them.

u301.description: Marks the second half of ancient Egyptian deity names, especially 'Amun', 'Atum', and 'Sobek' (plus related divine-name tokens).

u302.description: Adjectives/adverbs marking superlatives and 'first/only/last' uniqueness (first, only, highest, ever, up to), often in 'the X ... to have/that/ever' constructions.

u303.description: The token marks a word that is part of a compound proper name or compound noun phrase, nearly always the second element of a multi-word group name (e.g. 'upperparts', 'wheelchair basketball', 'women's national', 'United States', 'Fazlur Rahman', 'England national', 'Wales at', '19 43').

u304.description: Mid-word letter fragments (generally the second or later character inside a token), often part of names/terms like 'Reichskommissariat', 'coup d'état', 'Gloire/Gueydon', 'Sheffield United', 'Dilwale', etc.

u305.description: Possessive 's or possessive/attributive markers linking a noun to what follows (including 's, possessive pronouns, and related determiners/quantifiers)

u306.description: The unit fires on multiple unrelated patterns: 'Run Run Rudolph' titles, names (Rudin, Vidyadharas/Guadalupe), numeric conversions (30 feet to 9.1 m), chemical equations with '+' and '→', and function words like 'every/any/some/what'.

u307.description: It responds to the second half of a proper noun or compound name, i.e., the token completing names/terms (usually right after a capitalized word or name part).

u308.description: Words expressing freedom, discretion, or unrestricted choice (discretion, free, freedom, creative, power, whatever, want, wide), often in the phrase 'freedom/discretion to/width to'.

u309.description: Acronyms and multi-word proper-name units, especially at the point of their first or subsequent token such as RAAF, RIAA, Recording Industry Association, and 'Player' in MVP.

u310.description: Word-internal prefixes/substrings that are homographic or near-homographic across unrelated words: medical/technical roots (polyneuropathy, nerves), taxonomic prefixes (Neo-, Near Eastern, Neot-), and French-origin 'née', often mid-word rather than at token start.

u311.description: The marked tokens span several unrelated roles: sports statistics (games, ERA, goaltender), units of measurement (inches, in, years), and a few lexical/grammatical continuations (following, trade, no), with no single unifying concept.

u312.description: The marked tokens span unrelated contexts: Thai script/transliteration boundaries, measurements/unit numbers, hyphenated compound or numeric fragments, and occasional English word/pronoun positions, with no single shared concept.

u313.description: Marks a comma (occasionally another punctuation mark) that introduces a follow-up clause, restatement, or elaboration, especially after a quantity or list where a breakdown, subset, or additional number is given (e.g., "N, of which...", "N, both...", "N, six of them...", "N, M0 through to M7").

u314.description: The marked tokens span diverse roles: numbers/dates, prepositions (in, of), punctuation (comma, period, newline), words like space, the, Census, New, were, are, three, draw, standard, and a subword (solic), with no single shared concept.

u315.description: The unit responds to capitalized name/entity tokens, typically the beginning of a proper name (especially 'Creutz', but also other names, months, nationalities, and places).

u316.description: The unit fires on many different tokens—parenthetical/conversion numbers, song-title words, interjections, and abbreviations—with no single shared job.

u317.description: The marked token is usually a low-content function word or the tail of a word, appearing in diverse contexts without a single clear concept.

u318.description: Marks the boundary mid-word at the start of a capitalized proper noun or technical term, especially in names, titles, and multiword entities.

u319.description: predicting the next token in common multiword phrases or proper names (e.g., 'coming back', 'Blue Jackets', 'Come to an End')

u320.description: The active token varies widely: dates/years, the word 'for' in award nominations, suffix fragments like 'oc' in iconoclasts or 's' in possessive, and words like 'median'/'nominee', so no single shared job is evident.

u321.description: The marked tokens reflect unrelated patterns: the word 'half' in sports scores/time, 'a' in 'half a', contractions like 'don't/didn't', and miscellaneous word-completions such as 'Confucian', 'Glut', 'Jesuits', 'Temptations', and 'currently'.

u322.description: The unit responds to the first part of a multi-token proper name, especially a Romanian given name like Mihai/Mircea or a person's first name (e.g., Mihai, Merkley, Jon, Lasker, Arkadelphia).

u323.description: The unit responds to tokens starting with capital letters in the middle of proper names, especially the first letters of surnames, place names, or team names (e.g., 'Vas', 'Sab', 'Ay', 'Cas', 'Haz', 'Kas', 'Kaz', 'Downloadable').

u324.description: The token is mainly the second digit of decade-year ranges (especially 1970s, 1960s, 1990s, and 1940), with closely related offshoots like Jr., Studio, 's, –, and other continuation tokens.

u325.description: The marked token is typically the first part of a larger word or name (a word-internal boundary), often at the start of an inflected or compound form or proper name.

u326.description: Completes or continues common multi-word expressions with 'more/less/no ... than/longer/yet'—mainly the comparative phrase 'more than' and the temporal negations 'no longer'/'not yet'.

u327.description: The token sits at or near hyphens/punctuation in compound words, units, and numeric ranges, especially the first part of an '@-@' or decimal point before the next segment.

u328.description: Marks the boundary where a compound word or multi-word expression is split by subword tokenization (e.g. Super|bike, Par|alympics, thrombo|cytopenia, Formula|One, Stein|berg, etc.).

u329.description: Marked tokens are heterogeneous parts of dates, numbers, compounds, and function words with no single shared concept or next-word pattern.

u330.description: The marked tokens are heterogeneous (comparative 'better', auxiliary 'has/have', verbs like 'tolerate/winning/drowned', 'which/to', etc.) with no single concept, pattern, or next-word role clearly unifying them.

u331.description: The token 'also' (and closely related 'same'/'that'/'those'/'it') marking an additive or repeated-reference connective, generally introducing an additional related fact.

u332.description: The marked tokens are mostly a mix of prepositions/conjunctions (of, to, on, from), a comma, numbers/dates, and assorted content words, with no single coherent linguistic role.

u333.description: Tokens are mid-word pieces of recognizable proper names, mostly Polish names/history plus the Gatorade brand, so the unit responds to proper-noun name fragments.

u334.description: The unit fires on the token that immediately follows a word ending in a consonant sound, marking the onset of the next word or punctuation.

u335.description: Sentence-initial positions, especially the start of a new sentence after a period or line break.

u336.description: Mixed contexts: some mark 'fire/fired/firing' gun actions, others mark 'then' (former role), sports 'Cup', and assorted word-part completions like 'ethyl', 'enh', 'op', 'cal', 'mus', 'thal', 'my'.

u337.description: Tokens that are the first word of a multi-word proper name or established phrase, especially 'Old' in titles like Old Wine/Old World/Old Men/Old Quarter and 'Cold' in Coldrum, plus closely related first elements of set phrases like nomen dubium and New Kingdom/Britain.

u338.description: The unit responds to the start of a complement or prepositional phrase, especially 'that' clauses, 'of' phrases, and 'to'/'with'/'for'/'seems'/'evidence'/'justify' patterns that introduce subordinate content.

u339.description: The token is always at the start of an 'sc'/'Sc' letter sequence, most often words beginning with or containing 'sc' (scuttling, scrapping, Scouting, Scutari, Scrooge, scleroderma, Scop, Scarface), with related offshoots like 'slo' (roof), 'So' (Soir), 'Ep' (Epiphany), 'Pot' (Potowatami), and 'ä' (skärgårdsfregatter).

u340.description: It responds to sports-transaction and stats contexts, especially the token completing phrases about trades, saves, and field-goal/goal/shot terms.

u341.description: The marked tokens are mostly prepositions, possessives, articles, numbers, and word fragments with no clear shared linguistic or next-word role.

u342.description: Opens a parenthetical or clause with units/figures, often following a measurement or name to supply a conversion or clarification.

u343.description: The marked tokens span unrelated roles: part of the phrase 'contents of their granules', possessive determiners like 'its/their', name continuations such as 'Cabrera/Garrido', and varied common words like 'the/of/release', with no single shared concept.

u344.description: The unit activates on the first token of a capitalized proper name or compound that continues a multi-token entity, especially names ending in -m, -p, -Com-/Pay-/Pier- etc., i.e., it marks the start of a place, person, organization, or brand name within a larger noun phrase.

u345.description: activates on the first letter of proper nouns (names and place names), often at the start of a capitalized word or letter that follows a space or punctuation

u346.description: Past-tense verbs, especially irregular or weak verb forms marking completed actions (shot, lays, played, shown, seeking, entered, aired, plays).

u347.description: Digits inside four-digit years in parenthetical citations and references (often early or mid year digits, e.g. 20 in 2002, 19 in 1994).

u348.description: Marks an internal letter or word-internal position within a proper name or technical term, often anticipating a specific suffix or completing a known name.
